newsitem.title: USA: Glickman defends proposed meat inspector fees.
newsitem.headline: Glickman defends proposed meat inspector fees.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman Thursday acknowledged there may be industry resistance to proposed meat inspection fees but said they were essential to ensure food safety.
The Clinton administration has proposed $390 million in user fees in its FY98 budget that would cover the cost of putting federal inspectors in meat, poultry and egg plants.

"I know it's going to be tough," Glickman told a news conference on USDA's budget. "But I do not believe over the long term we can properly protect the health and safety of the American people by doing business exactly the same way we've done before."
Glickman said budget constraints make it necessary to ask industry to chip in and that the department would work to ensure the fees were "fair".

"I have a role to convince the American people and the Congress that without this kind of fee arrangement which I'm sure industry will probably fight, at least initially, without it we jeopardize the long-term safety of our meat and poultry industry," he said.
